question: Which cranial nerve supplies the main feeling and sensation to the mouth and teeth?
explanation: The trigeminal nerve supplies sensory fibers to the teeth, gums, and lining of the mouth. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of saliva in digestion while food is still in the mouth?

options.A: Emulsifying large fat globules for absorption
options.C: Absorbing simple sugars directly through the mucosa

explanation: Salivary amylase starts breaking down starches into simpler sugars right inside the mouth. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the medical name for a fungal mouth infection that causes white patches you can wipe off?
explanation: Candida overgrowth causes white patches on the mouth lining that can leave a bleeding surface when scraped off. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the main difference between simple gum inflammation (gingivitis) and advanced gum disease?

options.A: Gingivitis is always caused by viral agents
options.C: Gingivitis only affects the hard palate

explanation: Gingivitis only affects the gum tissue and is reversible, whereas advanced gum disease destroys the supporting jawbone. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which type of early mouth lesion has a higher risk of turning into cancer?
explanation: Erythroplakia shows up as a red patch and carries a higher risk of turning into cancer compared to white patches. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient has a white patch on their tongue that will not scrape off. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Document the lesion and refer the patient for biopsy
options.B: Instruct the patient to apply antiseptic mouthwash daily
options.C: Reassure the patient that it will resolve spontaneously
options.D: Scrape the lesion vigorously to remove the plaque

explanation: Persistent white patches that cannot be scraped off need a professional check and a biopsy to rule out cancer. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is a tissue biopsy needed when checking certain mouth sores?

options.A: To evaluate the production of saliva
options.C: To measure systemic blood glucose levels
options.D: To clear bacterial infections in the gums

explanation: Looking at a tissue sample under a microscope is the most reliable way to check for cancer cells. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which imaging test is commonly used to check if an oral cancer has spread to the jawbone?
explanation: Panoramic X-rays give a wide view of the upper and lower jaw to check for bone damage. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which type of medicine is standard treatment for an oral fungal infection like thrush?
explanation: Antifungal medications target and destroy the fungal cells causing the infection. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h5)

question: How does viscous lidocaine help patients who have painful mouth sores?

options.C: Killing the bacteria causing the ulceration
options.D: Shrinking inflamed blood vessels in the gums

explanation: Viscous lidocaine acts as a local numbing agent so the patient can eat and swallow with less discomfort. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the most important thing a nurse must monitor right after major mouth surgery?
explanation: Swelling in the mouth after surgery can easily block the airway, making breathing safety the top priority. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the medical term for the surgical removal of all or part of the tongue?
explanation: A glossectomy is the surgical removal of tongue tissue, often done to treat cancer. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why are lukewarm, non-spicy foods advised for patients with open sores in the mouth?

options.A: They directly eliminate fungal pathogens in the saliva
options.B: They harden tooth enamel against future decay
options.C: They stimulate increased production of digestive enzymes
options.D: They prevent chemical and thermal irritation to raw mucosa

explanation: Hot or acidic foods burn and sting raw mouth tissues, whereas bland, lukewarm foods are much easier to tolerate. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h7)

question: A patient with sore gums asks how to change their daily cleaning routine. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Stop all oral hygiene until the bleeding stops completely
options.B: Rinse exclusively with concentrated lemon juice daily
options.C: Brush gently with a soft-bristled brush and floss daily
options.D: Use a hard-bristled brush to aggressively scrub away plaque

explanation: Gentle brushing and daily flossing clear away plaque without hurting tender, inflamed gums. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h7)
